title: Compare API object ownership
license_review: MIT source/license bytes matched the immutable image. Runtime dependencies and Alpine/Python retain their own image notices; see the recorded package inventory. No upstream source or image is redistributed in the Ascend wheel.
objective: Compare owner, another user, and unauthenticated access to the same object in vulnerable and corrected configurations.
instructions: Open the two loopback endpoints shown by local-lab show; /ui provides the upstream API description. Each starts with name1/pass1 and name2/pass2. Create a book as name1, compare its secret response as name1, name2 and an anonymous caller in both configurations, and write observations in notes.txt. The fixed profile corrects this selected ownership behavior; other VAmPI weaknesses remain. local-lab check repeats independent reference probes, including legitimate controls. A passing comparison checks the environments, not your explanation or independent solving. Stop/resume retains the database; reset starts a separate attempt. Export keeps the structured local report; finish destroys both databases and retains your notes.

measurements.download_scope: Pinned compressed OCI layers/config plus selected assets; shared layers may already be cached. Not a packet-level traffic measurement.
measurements.disk_scope: Observed host filesystem delta at lifecycle checkpoints; includes Docker storage and unrelated concurrent filesystem activity. Image and volume bytes are also recorded independently.

measurements.scope: Real image source audit, six comparison probes, wrong fixed configuration, loopback/non-root/limits inspection, cross-origin refusal, volume persistence through stop/resume, export/finish, missing container, busy volume failure/retry, killed companion, hard expiry and idempotent cleanup. SQLite exhaustion at the 16 MiB limit, request size bound, error for a missing target, and acquired-image cache cleanup.

isolation_scope: Two non-root HTTP targets with debugger disabled on an internal network, reached through a fixed-destination loopback proxy on a separate front network. The proxy has no caller-selected destinations or CONNECT. Read-only roots, no host mounts/socket, resource/database limits, and a CHOWN-only volume initializer. Not a sandbox for arbitrary shells or submitted code.
